item.title: 'Everyone knew': Ex-Australia bowler Chadd Sayers fires fresh salvo at Pat Cummins over sandpaper scandal
item.description: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has challenged Pat Cummins’ version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, backing Usman Khawaja’s claim that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper during the South Africa tour. Sayers, who was part of the touring squad, said he believed every player was aware of what was happening. He also disagreed with Cummins’ statement that there was no team discussion about taking collective responsibility after the incident. “I’m comfortable sitting here … that I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used,” Sayers told SEN radio on Sunday. “I’m not taking sides. I’m neutral in all this, I’m just trying to tell my side of the story and what I believe happened.” The controversy has returned to the spotlight following Khawaja’s autobiography, in which he claimed the entire team knew about the sandpaper plan and suggested Australia had used ball-tampering methods even before the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s allegations as “complete nonsense” during a press conference on Friday. However, Sayers was unhappy with how the Australian captain addressed the issue, particularly his personal comments about Khawaja. “I didn’t like how he [Cummins] did go at Usman and got personal. I probably get why but I don’t think it needed to happen.” Sayers recalls team meeting after scandal Sayers also remembered a lengthy discussion among players after the incident came to light. This contradicts Cummins’ version of events. “We all sat in the change rooms after that day’s play, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, and just talked about what had happened and where to next,” Sayers said. He added that he was relieved the matter was finally being discussed openly after years of players having to remain silent. Warner questions Cricket Australia's investigation Meanwhile, former vice-captain David Warner has again questioned Cricket Australia’s investigation, alleging that important information was withheld from him. Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, was punished following the scandal. Warner claimed he was never informed that bowlers had been interviewed during the investigation and questioned why the governing body had not shared all the evidence with him before he accepted his punishment. “Just to clarify ‘As far as I am aware’ was the POINT,” he wrote on Instagram. “I was never told the bowlers had been interviewed or provided statements. “That information would’ve been pretty useful when I was forced to make decisions back in 2018. Why weren’t we given all the evidence by CA?”

item.title: McIlroy wins record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title
item.description: Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy in action at the DP World Tour Championship golf tournament at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai (Fadel SENNA) Rory McIlroy won his eighth Race to Dubai title to tie the record of Scotland's Colin Montgomerie after a dramatic final round of the season-ending $10 million DP World Tour Championship on Sunday. The tournament itself was a runaway win for England's Tyrrell Hatton (66) but all eyes were on the fascinating battle between McIlroy and Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, playing a group behind. It all came down to the 18th hole, where McIlroy made a disappointing par to finish on 10-under par, but that was good enough for a solo second place. That took his ranking points to 5,044.86. Chacarra also could not get a birdie on the final hole and closed with a 69 for a tied third place at eight-under alongside Finland's Oliver Lindell (65). The European number one crown was secured with a bogey-free round of five-under par 67, but it all came down to the par-4 16th hole, where he hit a magnificent second shot to a foot for the decisive birdie. McIlroy started with a birdie, but the momentum seemed to have been halted over the next four holes, when he burnt the edge on three but could not get a second birdie. He then picked up three shots over the next four holes, but Chacarra kept him in sight with four birdies in his first eight holes. When McIlroy could not make a birdie on the par-5 14th hole, Chacarra was leading the projected ranking by a mere 0.1 point. Hatton finally finished with seven birdies against a solitary mistake on the third hole on a day when he again dazzled with brilliant short iron and wedge play. The win was worth $3 million and he also climbed to third in the Race to Dubai behind McIlroy and Chacarra, his career best finish. According to Caught Offside, Liverpool are among the clubs monitoring the Frenchman, with Manchester United also watching closely as Manchester City push to the front of the queue. There is a familiar rhythm to stories like this. A young goalkeeper emerges in Ligue 1, carries himself with authority, shows composure in possession and suddenly the wealthiest clubs in Europe begin circling. Risser appears to fit that pattern neatly. He is said to have the frame, the calmness and the technical level that modern elite sides crave, especially those that ask their goalkeeper to do far more than stop shots. Building from the back remains central to how top sides want to play and succession planning in goal is one of the most delicate tasks in football. item.description: Chelsea see bid rejected for £25m La Liga star Chelsea Transfer News: Jose Antonio Morante Rejection Shows Betis Winger Has a Clear Plan Chelsea’s recruitment machine keeps scanning the market for young talent, and this time the trail led to Jose Antonio Morante. According to Metro, the Blues tried to make headway for the Real Betis winger, only to find the door closed by the player himself. That matters. Clubs can test the waters with agents and intermediaries all they like, but when a 19-year-old decides he would rather stay put and fight for minutes at his boyhood club, that tells you something about his priorities. Morante is not chasing the biggest badge in the room. He is chasing a football plan that suits him. Photo: IMAGO Jose Antonio Morante Chooses Real Betis Path Morante only broke into the Betis first team earlier this year and has made three senior appearances this season. On the surface, those numbers are modest. The context is more revealing. He is a teenager coming through at a serious club, and Betis clearly see value in him. Over the summer he raised his profile considerably with Spain’s UEFA European Under-19 Championship-winning side. A place in the Team of the Tournament and four goals, enough to finish as joint-top scorer, made him one of the standout names in his age group. Chelsea tracked him there and followed up with an approach during the summer window. The answer was no. By all accounts, Morante wants to establish himself as a first-team regular with Real Betis. It is a sensible call, and one plenty of young players could learn from. Real Betis Contract Underlines Chelsea Setback Betis moved quickly in July, tying Morante down until 2030. The new contract also includes a €30 million, £25m, release clause. That is not a token number. It is protection, leverage and a warning to anyone circling. Reports in Spain suggest Chelsea remained persistent. Persistence is fine. It does not change the reality that the player has chosen continuity over acceleration. For Chelsea, that is a miss, but not necessarily a damaging one. They have built a strategy around identifying emerging talent early. Some will say yes, some will not. item.title: Eugenio Chacarra’s immediate reaction after losing out to Rory McIlroy in the Race to Dubai
item.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images Rory McIlroy won a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown on Sunday after he finished in second place at the DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy posted a superb final round score of 67 to finish two strokes clear of his main rival for the season-long race, Eugenio Chacarra. The Northern Irishman’s second-place finish at the Earth Course secured his fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title. Rory McIlroy has now tied Colin Montgomerie with eight Race to Dubai crowns. It’s fair to say that the six-time major champion was nowhere near his best this week in Dubai, but he did enough to get the job done in the end. Getting that eighth order of merit title under his belt was so important for McIlroy, and now his attention will turn to breaking the record next year. Chacarra came so close to winning his first season-long race, and he gave a great account of himself throughout 2026. Eugenio Chacarra’s reaction after Rory McIlroy wins the Race to Dubai The race between McIlroy and Chacarra went right down to the wire , and the Spaniard deserves huge credit for pushing the Northern Irishman all the way. After his final round on Sunday, Chacarra was asked to share his feelings after just missing out on the order of merit title. “ Yeah, it was a good fight. I just came up short, “ he admitted. “ That’s the beauty of golf, Obviously, when you play with the best in the world. And he’s played here 14, 15 times, you knew it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did. “ Yeah, I played good. I fought hard. I knew it was going to be a long day and I tried my best. That’s all I can ask for myself to do and that’s what we did. “ As I said yesterday, it was a bonus, and I would say proud of the fight and proud to have a chance till the end. “ Chacarra then commented on the prospect of playing on the PGA Tour next year. “ Yeah, super excited. But I love the DP World Tour. It’s been so much for me and hopefully I can start good over there and come here as much as possible, “ he said.

item.title: Andres Iniesta heaps praise on Lamine Yamal – “Joy to have him as Barcelona and Spain player”
item.description: Andres Iniesta heaps praise on Lamine Yamal – “Joy to have him as Barcelona and Spain player” Lamine Yamal is no stranger to praises from some of the legends of football, having established himself as arguably football’s biggest and most talented young star since Lionel Messi about two decades ago. Having already won the FIFA World Cup and the European Championship with Spain, Yamal has recently received praise from none other than Andres Iniesta. The Barcelona legend has pointed out how Yamal has continued to better himself at every turn and is now one of the unique players in world football. What Iniesta said about Yamal Yamal is growing in confidence every year. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Speaking to DAZN, Iniesta said Yamal has the potential to become a unique star and praised his hard work. “There’s no doubt that Lamine has incredible talent. It’s in his hands to become a unique player,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Iniesta also feels grateful that Yamal is a Spanish and Barcelona player, rather than being a foreign talent. “I hope he continues to improve every year, keeps working on himself and makes the team better. For me, as a Barcelona fan and as a Spaniard, it’s a privilege and a joy to have Lamine playing for Barcelona and the national team,” he added. Iniesta praises Spain national team Iniesta believes Yamal can achieve bigger things. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Apart from his praise on Yamal, Iniesta is also happy with the direction the Spain national team is heading under Luis de la Fuente. The Barcelona legend labelled Spain as one of the favourites to win the upcoming international competitions. “Of course, Spain are among the favourites because of what they represent, the squad they have and the fact that they come into it having won, ” he said. The former midfielder pointed out that the connection between the Spanish players and the technical staff has been second to none. “I see a very strong connection between the players and the coaching staff, and that’s a big advantage, ” he concluded. This Spain team will be in action this evening as they take on England, a game Lamine Yamal is likely to be a part of after missing out against Czechia.

item.description: Australia have now won 23 consecutive World Cup matches since 2008 [Getty Images] Australia (24) 32 Tries: Martin 2, Bostock 2, Best, Trbojevic Goals: Munster 4 New Zealand (6) 12 Tries: McLean, Papali'i Goals: Isaako 2 Same old story. Having started the Rugby League World Cup in unconvincing fashion, Australia once again showed why they are masters of peaking for the big occasion as they defeated New Zealand 32-12 to be crowned champions for a fourth consecutive occasion. And this was never really close as the green and gold juggernaut pressed repeat on what has become a familiar pattern - and a depressing one for all those that have attempted to stop them since the Kiwis triumphed in Brisbane in the 2008 showpiece. Despite being outplayed and outmuscled by Stacey Jones' side in an epic opening to this tournament on 15 October, Australia still edged to a 24-22 victory. And five weeks on from that pulsating contest - perhaps stung by some observers questioning their credentials - Kevin Walters' team delivered conclusive proof that they remain the remain the benchmark for all others to aspire to. They were simply untouchable in the first-half, with a demonstration of power and quality that carried them into a 24-6 advantage at the break and a long way towards victory - their 23rd successive win in World Cup matches since that loss 18 years ago. Back on the ground where New Zealand delivered one of the most seismic shocks the international game has ever seen, there was never a moment where history threatened to repeat itself in front of a sell-out 52,500 crowd. Jones' team admittedly played a part in their own downfall. Jamayne Isaako's error from the kick-off set the tone and Australia ruthlessly punished it with Liam Martin bundling over to score from their first attack with just 84 seconds on the clock. While a converted try from the youngest player on the pitch, Casey McLean, briefly brought New Zealand level it was all they had to show from a disappointing first 40 minutes, when they repeatedly gifted Australia possession and field position. Quick thinking from Reece Walsh and Bradman Best laid on an eighth try of the tournament for Jack Bostock. Bostock, who was recovering from knee reconstruction surgery this time 12 months ago, has been a revelation out wide for Australia. The 23-year-old Dolphins winger has excelled in defence and attack under the aerial ball and married it to a penchant for regularly contributing with key tries at the other end of the pitch. item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo © @MiamiHEAT/X Giannis Antetokounmpo continues to prove why he’s one of the Miami Heat’s most consistent performers. During Saturday’s 137-117 victory over the Detroit Pistons, Antetokounmpo recorded his 10th double-double of the season, finishing with 34 points and 14 rebounds, including a dazzling no-look, between-the-legs pass that left his teammates in awe. The highlight-reel play came in the first quarter when Giannis almost lost the ball after the Pistons sent a double-team his way. As he fell forward while trying to recover it, Giannis shuffled the ball between his legs to Klay Thompson, who buried the shot for his first of six 3-pointers on the night. Thompson couldn’t help but be in awe of what Giannis did and gave him high praise after the game. “People get enamored with his ability to run and dunk but my goodness, he’s like Magic at times with his vision,” Thompson said (via @TheHeatCentral). – Klay Thompson with high praise for Giannis passing https://t.co/ovyBFyjS00 — Heat Central (@TheHeatCentral) November 15, 2026 Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra echoed the same sentiment, saying: “We need a touch of Magic Johnson with him. He’s shouldering a ton of responsibility. He’s literally making this look easy… But he also has to make sure the offense has a flow. That means when there’s defenders loading up, bringing a third defender, oftentimes it’s that early kick-out that gets guys in a rhythm.” It was a brilliant play by the 31-year-old, who seems to get better with each passing game on his new team. item.title: “They Want More Money?” – Martina Navratilova Reacts to Sean Duffy’s Appeal To Congress to Fund Trump Administration’s Air Traffic Control Plan After FAA Groundstop
item.description: Martina Navratilova | © Imagn Former World No. 1 Martina Navratilova reacted to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s appeal to Congress for $50 billion in emergency funding for America’s air traffic control system following a nationwide FAA groundstop. The groundstop halted U.S. departures for over four hours on Friday. Duffy pointed to outdated technology as a reason for the disruption that delayed or canceled more than 14,000 flights. Speaking at a press conference at the White House, Duffy warned that these systems could keep failing if they are not completely replaced. “We have old, old switches, old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines,” Duffy said. “What went down was old, right? It was the old legacy equipment. It failed.” “This is an emergency. I want Congress to give us emergency funding,” Duffy added. “This is bipartisan. This is American. I want $50 billion.” However, Navratilova criticized the transportation secretary for requesting additional funds despite having already received a large budget. “And $11 billion of that money is still there, not having been used. And they want more money???” Congress had previously approved $12.5 billion for air traffic control modernization. At only 19 years old, Andreeva became the youngest WTA Finals finalist since Maria Sharapova in 2004. She won all three group stage matches in straight sets and saw off Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4. Navratilova praised Andreeva’s confidence, serving and ability to control rallies. The former World No. 1 also noted that Andreeva is making it difficult for opponents to find her weaknesses. “She’s just really confident right now,” Navratilova said. “She’s hit her sweet spot, and maybe playing back-to-back matches helps because you’ve built up that momentum and you can still feel it. She looks really sharp. It’s hard to find an opening against her because she’s serving big and mixing it up. She hits a 90 mph serve wide with a lot of slice, and then she hits 115 down the T. item.title: Rory McIlroy wins Race to Dubai title for record-equalling eighth time
item.description: Rory McIlroy has won the Race to Dubai title for a record-equalling eighth time, pipping Eugenio Chacarra to the crown. Spaniard Chacarra had held a slender 533.93-point lead over Masters champion McIlroy going into the season finale at Jumeirah Golf Estates. McIlroy, though, overturned that deficit after a blemish-free fourth round of 67 saw him finish on 10 under par, on his own in second, to take a fifth successive European tour crown, matching Colin Montgomerie ’s record of eight Order of Merit titles. Ryder Cup team-mate Tyrell Hatton , meanwhile, stormed to victory in Dubai, ending the day five shots ahead of second-placed McIlroy to round off a fantastic week. "Winning eight Order of Merits (now called Race to Dubai) was never in my list of goals growing up,” McIlroy said. "I remember Monty being a stalwart of the European tour and playing with him at the London Club in 2008, so to pull up alongside him and win eight of these means the world to me. "I'm proud to be European and part of this tour." Visibly choked up, McIlroy revealed that his dad Gerry has been in hospital since undergoing "a huge operation in September" and said his triumph was for him. Rory McIlroy won the Race to Dubai title as Tyrell Hatton triumphed at the DP World Championship (Getty) He also reflected on the drama of the day and insisted he wasn’t aware of how “back and forth” the title fight with Chacarra was until he reached the 16th. "When I walked to the 16th green I saw Eugenio [Chacarra] was projected one, and when I walked off after my birdie I was projected one,” he added. "Eugenio played pretty good, but none of the chasing pack made a move and thankfully everything fell my way. "I pride myself in my consistency. I finished third last week, second this week. I feel like I've done a good job in recent years of not playing my way out of tournaments like I did earlier in my career." It was heartbreak for Chacarra, who needed to win the tournament to make sure he fended off McIlroy, as well as potentially several other big hitters in the chasing pack. Eugenio Chacarra was pipped to the crown (Getty) However, a final round of 69, which featured six birdies but also three bogeys either side of the turn, saw him come up just short at eight under in a tie for third, with other scores in the final groups also going McIlroy’s way. "It was a good fight. I just came out short. That's the beauty of golf,” he said. "Obviously, when you play with the best in the world. And McIlroy's played here 14, 15 times, you knew it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did. "I played good. I fought. I knew it was going to be a long day, and I tried my best. That's all I can ask for myself to do and that's what we did."

George Groves makes his pick for Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia The biggest question ahead of Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia is: what does “The Bronze Bomber” have left? Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) has built a fearsome reputation, with many calling him one of the biggest punchers in the history of the heavyweight division. Opetaia (31-0, 24 KOs) has dazzled at cruiserweight while chasing the biggest fights. He is still the current Ring magazine champ and former two-time cruiserweight world champion. His best performances have come against David Nyika and Mairis Briedis. Speaking on the Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia bout, Groves gave a knockout prediction to Pro Boxing Fans: “I think that Opetaia wins. item.description: The expectations for the Cleveland Browns were fairly mixed coming into the season. There was a lot of optimism surrounding the young talent on the roster, but there were still many questions about the quarterback position and what the team would be able to accomplish offensively. The offensive line, in particular, has had some good moments, but it has consistently struggled to protect the quarterback and has made it difficult for the run game to get going. This has made it difficult for the offense to perform at a high level. Costly mistakes have been another big issue for this team, as they lead the league in penalties this season with 82 . This comes out to 9.1 penalties per game. These costly mistakes put the offense in difficult yardage situations and make it harder to move the ball down the field. Especially in close games, a few penalties can really make the difference between winning and losing. item.title: Haaland 'incredibly happy' at City and focused on form, not sanctions
item.description: Norway's Erling Haaland (r) scores his team's third goal from the penalty spot during the UEFA Nations League Group A4 soccer match between Norway and Wales at Ullevaal Stadion. (is associated with: «Haaland 'incredibly happy' at City and focused on form, not sanctions») Nick Potts/PA Wire/dpa Erling Haaland says he is “incredibly happy” at Manchester City and his focus is on performing and not on the potential sanctions against the club. City have appealed after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations. The club could face heavy sanctions, including huge points deductions or demotion, should the verdict be upheld. Haaland was asked about the case after Norway’s 3-1 Nations League victory over Wales in Oslo on Saturday, in which he scored his 66th goal in 60 international appearances. “This is a question I struggle to answer, because it’s a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City,” Haaland told Norwegian broadcaster TV2. “Am I supposed to answer that? I don’t really know. It’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t know that much about it. “To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. “I think that says everything about the matter. I’m a City player and I’m incredibly happy there.” Asked if the situation affects his City future, Haaland replied: “I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said I signed a long-term contract in 2024. “I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. “I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. “I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren’t going so well in the Premier League, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham (on Saturday).” City maintain they have a “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” to support their case, despite being found guilty by an independent commission in September. The commission’s damning findings included breaches relating to the concealment of funding worth more than £830 million ($1.098 billion) over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. Haaland said the period under investigation happened before he joined City, and in the interview he painstakingly pointed out each stage of his football journey during that time. item.title: McIlroy wins record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Northern Irish professional golfer Rory McIlroy reacts during a preview day ahead of The 154th Open Championship at Royal Birkdale in Southport. (is associated with: «McIlroy wins record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown») David Davies/PA Wire/dpa Rory McIlroy edged out Eugenio Chacarra to claim a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title with a second-place finish at the DP World Tour Championship, where Tyrrell Hatton sealed a five-shot victory on Sunday. Spaniard Chacarra had held a slender 533.93-point lead over Masters champion McIlroy going into the season finale at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai. McIlroy, though, overturned that deficit after a blemish-free fourth round of 67 saw him finish on 10 under par, on his own in second, to take a fifth successive Race to Dubai crown, matching Colin Montgomerie’s record of eight Order of Merit titles. Chacarra had needed to win the tournament to make sure he fended off McIlroy, as well as potentially several other big hitters in the chasing pack. However, a final round of 69, which featured six birdies but also three bogeys either side of the turn, saw him come up just short at eight under in a tie for third, with other scores in the final groups also going McIlroy’s way. Englishman Hatton secured his first DP World Tour Championship title at 15 under, pulling clear following his closing round of 66, which saw him take third place in the overall Race to Dubai standings.

item.title: After winning the Ballon d’Or, Harry Kane says he’s ready to be a midfielder
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 12: Harry Kane of England raises the Ballon D'or trophy as he acknowledges the fans ahead of the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between England and Croatia at Wembley Stadium on November 12, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Sebastian Frej/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Harry Kane was awarded the Ballon d’Or for his exemplary season at Bayern Munich, one of the arguments in his favor was his all-round game. Under Vincent Kompany, Kane does not function as a regular striker, instead preferring to drop deep and make splitting passes like a quarterback. So, how about moving into midfield permanently? “That’s something I’d like to try at some point,” said Kane, when asked if he wanted a deeper role someday (via @iMiaSanMia ). “Even as a youngster at Tottenham, I played in midfield and in various different positions. When I started becoming a regular starter in Tottenham’s first team under Mauricio Pochettino, he saw me as a number 9 because I was scoring goals and constantly making runs in behind the defense.” “Then José Mourinho came along and probably took my game to another level because he gave me a lot of freedom. I knew that passing was one of my greatest strengths and that, when I dropped deeper, I was also good at receiving and controlling the ball under pressure. That season, I won both the Premier League Playmaker Award and the Golden Boot.” “Since joining Bayern, Vinnie and our style of play have given us a lot of freedom. That applies not just to me, but to other players as well. We can drop deeper, even into defensive areas, and influence the game from there. Over the past few years, that freedom, together with my increasingly good understanding of the game, has helped me develop enormously. For me, it’s great to know that I can continue doing all of that while still scoring goals. After all, last season I scored more goals than ever before in my career. That shows there isn’t just one way to play football or score goals. There are many different possibilities.” Kane has already taken a back seat in scoring these past few weeks, instead racking up assists every game. Fans of FC Bayern are a little bewildered by the change, though nothing has fundamentally changed in the way he interprets his game. If this is the beginning of a shift in how the England captain plays for club and country, maybe the next Ballon d’Or will be won by a midfielder. Join the conversation! item.description: Former Manchester City Defender Questions Enzo Maresca's Structure Amid Ongoing Problems What are Man City fans expecting from the 2026-27 season? City entered the November international break off the back of three Premier League defeats - against Aston Villa , Brighton and Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest - as Maresca navigates his side's first blip in form since the Italian succeeded Pep Guardiola as manager in June. The Blues started the 2026-27 campaign in blistering form, winning their first seven Premier League games and showing all the early signs of a squad that could pose a strict challenge to reigning champions Arsenal for the league title. However, Manchester City 's backline has struggled for form of late and Gianluigi Donnarumma has also been letting in goals for fun, leading to subdued run of form for the Blues in the league in the last month. Maresca has defended Donnarumma and co but admitted that there are problems he needs to solve in the international break, with City returning to action at the Etihad Stadium against Fulham on Saturday 21 November. In an interview with Betway , former Manchester City and England defender Joleon Lescott gave his two cents on the Sky Blues' chances in the Premier League title race. "City aren't on a great run at the moment, but I've seen enough from them to know they'll pick up the pace again at some point," Lescott said. "My only concern with regards to the Premier League title for City is whether Arsenal will fall off with the lead they now have. "Teams can go on runs, but I don't see Arsenal losing three games on the bounce any time soon, and those games against Arsenal for City are now must-wins for me. "As I say, there's enough there for Manchester City to win games and go on a run, but they just aren't doing it consistently at the moment." Why are Man City struggling in defence this season? Continuing in his discussion, Lescott was also able to put his finger on what he believes are the root causes of City's ongoing defensive problems, as Maresca's rearguard continues to concede goals at an alarming rate. "When we talk about teams conceding goals, we put the blame on the defenders usually, but it isn't that for Manchester City in my opinion," the former centre-half added. "I think it's the structure of the whole team, and the way they are set up, which is exposing a few players, and some of the defenders are having to defend in areas of the pitch they don't want to be.
